clue.text: A partner out of place is cut off

indicators.note: A partner sits out of, i.e. around, the word for place, so the second piece is held within the first

parts.note: a partner is a mate, so 'a partner' gives A plus MATE
to place something is to put it down

explanation.surface: Someone whose partner has gone missing is left on their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' signals that A MATE wraps round PUT. The answer is a verb, so 'is' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To amputate a limb is to sever it surgically from the body.

clue.text: Heartless poet performed

indicators.note: a heartless word loses its central letter, here one of the middle pair of the poet's name

parts.note: John Donne was the English metaphysical poet

explanation.surface: A cold, unfeeling versifier gave a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes one N from the middle of DONNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done has been carried out or performed, as in a deed already accomplished.

clue.text: Considerable rise with hazard for old lags

indicators.note: in a down clue, a rise means the word reads upwards, so its letters are turned round

parts.note: considerable means big
to hazard money is to bet it

explanation.surface: A big increase in gambling among former prisoners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns BIG into GIB. The definition is loose: a gibbet was the gallows where old criminals ('lags' is British slang for convicts) were hanged.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallows-like post on which executed criminals were hung was meant for hardened offenders of old.

clue.text: Blame me for designing inlaid ornament

indicators.note: designing the letters of the first two words means arranging them into a fresh pattern

explanation.surface: Accept the blame for designing a decorative inlay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designing' rearranges BLAMEME; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An emblema is a decorative inlaid piece, as in mosaic work or metal inlay.

clue.text: Composer lifts side overhead

annotationWithheld.why: Composer lifts side overhead (8): per the fifteensquared blog the parse is NESS (head, headland) inside TEAM (side) reversed, so the single word 'overhead' is both the container indicator 'over' and the fodder 'head'.

clue.text: Furniture items, one slightly damaged, for a good cause

indicators.note: one of the two pieces of furniture is knocked about a little, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: a chair is one item of furniture
a table is the other item of furniture

explanation.surface: Selling off slightly battered furniture to raise money for a charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Furniture items' gives two pieces, CHAIR and TABLE; 'one slightly damaged' scrambles CHAIR into CHARI.
explanation.definitionFit: Charitable work or giving is done in support of a worthy cause.

clue.text: Stingers make one dance wildly

indicators.note: wildly signals that the letters of one and dance are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Being stung makes a person leap about frantically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges I plus DANCE; 'make' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cnidae are the stinging cells of jellyfish and related creatures, also called nematocysts.

clue.text: This might need a doctor — none within miles, unfortunately

definitions.text: This might need a doctor — none within miles, unfortunately

indicators.note: within shows the doctor and the nothing are placed inside the scrambled distance word
unfortunately suggests things have gone awry, so the letters of miles are disordered

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree
none is nothing, the letter O

explanation.surface: A medical emergency far from help, with no doctor anywhere near.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' scrambles the distance word, and 'within' sets the doctor and the zero inside after its first letter. As an &lit the whole clue describes the condition; the blog notes some words work twice.
explanation.definitionFit: An embolism, a blood clot or air bubble blocking a vessel, is a medical emergency that calls for a physician.

clue.text: City set in layers after a time

indicators.note: the layers come after the opening pair of letters in the answer

parts.note: hens are birds that lay eggs, so layers

explanation.surface: A city built up in strata over a long period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layers' is not strata but egg-layers, HENS; 'set in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital city of Greece.

clue.text: Parson's duty to smoke?

definitions.meaning: the ... of souls is a priest's spiritual charge over a parish
to smoke fish or meat is to preserve it, one way of curing it

explanation.surface: A vicar's obligation to light up a pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: Two senses of one word: a clergyman's charge over a parish, and preserving food by smoking.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate's charge is a cure of souls; curing meat over smoke preserves it.

clue.text: Protection from fall of American commerce after party backing

indicators.note: the American commerce comes after the reversed party in the answer
backing means the party word is read from the back, so its letters run in reverse

parts.note: Lab is short for the UK Labour Party
commerce is trade

explanation.surface: A political party propping up a measure to protect the US economy from collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses LAB to BAL. 'fall' suggests an economic slump, but it is a literal fall from a height.
explanation.definitionFit: A balustrade is a railing on a stair or balcony that stops people from tumbling over.

clue.text: Sign of vehicle legislation

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
an act of Parliament is a piece of legislation

explanation.surface: A traffic sign put up under a new motoring law.
explanation.walkthrough: An old Shakespearean-era word, not in every dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Caract is an archaic word for a mark or distinguishing character, so a sign.

clue.text: Middle East alliance to be cultivated without right to contradict

parts.note: arable land is land fit to be farmed

indicators.note: without signals the abbreviation for right is dropped from the word for contradicting

parts.note: to argue is to contradict someone

explanation.surface: A regional alliance formed to farm land without anyone daring to object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes R out of ARGUE, leaving AGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arab League is the regional organisation of Arab states in the Middle East and North Africa.

clue.text: Fellow reported relaxing with Sirenians

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: reported means the word for relaxing is to be heard, not read, giving a near sound-alike

parts.note: relaxing is being at ease

explanation.surface: A man said to be lounging about with sea creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' turns AT EASE into its sound-alike ATEES; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Manatees, the sea cows, belong to the order Sirenia, the group named after the sirens.

clue.text: How to make grandee enraged or …

definitions.text: How to make grandee enraged or …

parts.words: How to make grandee enraged or
parts.note: the clue asks what you would do to the letters of grandee to turn it into enraged: jumble them, the very verb that also means drive mad

explanation.surface: Advice on how to infuriate a nobleman, running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the next clue, where 'turning potty' continues the sense of driving someone mad. Grandee and enraged are both scrambles of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to throw into disorder, whether letters or a person's mind, so both readings fit.

clue.text: Bloomer makes Roundhead lose head for good

indicators.note: the first letter is swapped out in favour of the abbreviation for good, so the head changes

parts.note: Oliver Cromwell led the Roundheads, Parliament's side in the English Civil War

explanation.surface: A gardener's mistake makes a Puritan leader lose his head for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose head for good' replaces the C of CROMWELL with G (good). 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flowering plant, and 'for good' seems to mean permanently.
explanation.definitionFit: Gromwell is a flowering plant of the borage family, so a bloomer in the botanical sense.

clue.text: … turning potty preceded getting shut up

indicators.note: turning means the word for potty is flipped so it reads in the other direction

parts.note: potty means crazy, which in slang is bats
to have preceded is to have led

explanation.surface: Someone going mad and then being locked away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses BATS to STAB. The ellipsis continues from the previous clue, but the clue stands alone; 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stabled horse is shut up in its stall, so stabled means confined.

clue.text: Curse managerial salary?

parts.note: an exec, executive, is a manager
a rate of pay is a salary

explanation.surface: Grumbling about a boss's pay packet.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to denounce or call down curses upon someone.

clue.text: Stupefied by 20 in bed?

indicators.note: the muse is placed in the bed, splitting it before its last letter

parts.note: the answer to 20, Calliope, is a muse

explanation.surface: Dazed after sharing a bed with a poet's inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: '20' refers to Calliope, the Muse of epic poetry; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bemused means bewildered or stupefied, unable to think clearly.

clue.text: Inspiration for poetry and everything one can manage without

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the managing word stands outside the others

parts.note: to cope is to be able to manage
everything is all
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A poet needs inspiration, and must cope without anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking: the managing word stands round the other two.
explanation.definitionFit: Calliope is the Muse of epic poetry in Greek myth, a source of a poet's inspiration.

clue.text: You can count on a god abandoning church

indicators.note: abandoning signals the god's name gives up the abbreviation for church

parts.note: Bacchus is the Roman god of wine

explanation.surface: A believer you can rely on, though one deity has left the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' takes CH out of BACCHUS, leaving BACUS.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads used for counting, so something one literally counts on.

clue.text: Examples of relativity — complex science church leader rejected

indicators.note: complex suggests a tangle, so the remaining letters are scrambled
rejected signals the leading letter is thrown out of the word science
leader points to the first letter of church

explanation.surface: Einstein's relativity is explained through complicated science, with a clergyman's objections set aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' gives C (church), which 'rejected' removes from SCIENCE, and 'complex' rearranges SIENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nieces are relatives, so they illustrate relativity in the punning sense of family relations.

clue.text: Fresh air is said to be a reason for this

indicators.note: is said means the phrase for a new tune is spoken, so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: a fresh air is a new tune, a new ditty

explanation.surface: Naturists claim being outdoors in the open air is why they strip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' is a tune, not the atmosphere; 'this' points back to fresh air, which going unclothed lets you feel.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unclothed exposes the skin to the breeze, so it is a cause of feeling the open air.

clue.text: Found at law to be a possible cause of death

indicators.note: to be signals that the first three words are to become something else, rearranged into a new phrase

explanation.surface: A coroner's legal finding about how someone died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' rearranges FOUNDATLAW; the indicator is weak, as the blog notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatal wound is an injury that kills, so one possible way of dying.

clue.text: Begin without beginning to be sweet and sour

indicators.note: without beginning means the word for begin loses its opening letter

parts.note: to begin is to start

explanation.surface: A recipe step for a sweet-and-sour dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without beginning' drops the S of START. A tart is a sweet pastry dish, and tart also means sour.
explanation.definitionFit: A tart is a sweet dessert, and as an adjective tart means sharp or sour in taste.

clue.text: The last place to take part in bingo

indicators.note: taking part in the game means taking only a part of it, the opening portion

parts.note: tombola is a game of chance much like bingo

explanation.surface: Where someone ends up after playing bingo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take part in' keeps only TOMB from TOMBOLA, a raffle-style game like bingo; the surface sense of joining in a game misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomb is the grave, where one is laid at the very end of life.

clue.text: Reciprocal element reflected in typical autumn fashion

indicators.note: reflected means the run of letters is seen as in a mirror, back to front
an element is a component, so the answer is a run of letters forming part of the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: Seasonal styles of autumn mirrored in each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'element' points to LAUTUM inside typicAL AUTUMn, and 'reflected' turns it round; 'in' and 'fashion' only join the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutual means shared or felt by each towards the other, the same as reciprocal.

clue.text: Guess Gordius is in the end condition

indicators.note: the end of the word the means its last letter
the setter's self-reference goes in the middle of the word for condition

parts.note: a state is a condition
the setter Gordius says I am, contracted to I'm

explanation.surface: The setter guesses at the condition they will be in at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end' takes the final letter of 'the', and 'in' is the container signal; a setter's name standing for I'm is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to make a rough judgement or approximate reckoning, which is what guessing a figure means.
